role: Mechanical Engineering Intern — Pressure Vessel & Composite Structures
overview: Supporting the development of ruggedized Type III composite overwrapped pressure vessel (COPV) systems for high-pressure hydrogen storage applications. Working across nonlinear structural analysis, composite laminate modeling, autofrettage simulation, and standards-based design verification for safety-critical pressure vessel architectures.
bullets: Developed nonlinear finite element models of Type III COPVs to evaluate burst behavior, residual stress development, and structural performance under high-pressure loading conditions.
Performed composite laminate analysis and autofrettage simulations to support pressure vessel qualification and compliance with ISO 11119-2 requirements.

Contributed to structural verification activities through ANSYS Mechanical and ACP, validating composite load-sharing behavior and pressure vessel response against analytical and published reference data.

overview: Supported the structural development of a patented Type III composite hydrogen storage vessel by reconstructing simulation-ready CAD geometry and performing nonlinear structural analyses ahead of physical testing.
bullets: Reconstructed a complete simulation-ready CAD assembly from engineering drawings, enabling downstream structural analysis of a safety-critical pressure vessel system.
Performed nonlinear FEA across operating pressure ranges to evaluate stress and deformation behavior, supporting design verification prior to prototype testing.

overview: Conducted research on lattice-enhanced cold plate architectures for electronics cooling applications, using computational fluid dynamics to evaluate thermal performance and hydraulic resistance across a broad geometric design space.
bullets: Designed and generated BCC lattice cold plate architectures using nTopology and SolidWorks for advanced thermal management applications.
Performed CFD studies across 30 design variants to characterize thermal performance, flow behavior, and hydraulic resistance.
Established a validated thermal-hydraulic design space that identified key geometric parameters governing cooling effectiveness and pressure drop.

overview: Led the design, analysis, fabrication, and validation of a collapsible industrial pallet intended to reduce warehouse storage requirements while maintaining industrial load capacity and long-term durability.
bullets: Designed and optimized a collapsible steel pallet and validated structural performance through finite element analysis under a 1-ton design load.
Fabricated and assembled the prototype using sheet metal manufacturing and welding processes while applying GD&T principles to maintain dimensional accuracy.
Correlated physical load testing with simulation results to refine structural behavior, contributing to improved durability and reduced replacement costs.

company: Defence Research & Development Organisation - Centre for Airborne Systems
overview: Performed structural validation of an airborne avionics electronics rack and shock mount assembly for the Embraer ERJ-145, evaluating stress, deformation, and load transfer behavior under operational and emergency loading conditions.
bullets: Verified structural integrity of an avionics electronics rack under shock and vibration loading across operational and emergency flight conditions.
Evaluated shock mount behavior and load transmission between the rack and mounting structure as part of a system-level structural validation effort.

role: Leeds International Summer School — Fluid Dynamics in Theory and Practice
overview: Completed an intensive international program focused on fluid dynamics, hydraulic modeling, and real-world engineering applications of flow analysis.
bullets: Modeled flood behavior in the Akaki region of Ethiopia using HEC-RAS and historical hydrological data to analyze flood propagation and risk.
Applied fluid mechanics principles to a practical flood modeling project, evaluating flow behavior and water level predictions under varying conditions.
Participated in lectures and demonstrations led by Prof. Mark Trigg and Prof. Bokhove, including the Wetropolis physical flood model used to visualize rainfall, runoff, and extreme flood events.
